title_en: China Huarong Asset Management Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Baoshan Branch v. Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over a financial loan contract
ruling_gist_en: Commercial banks shall follow the principles of lawfulness and compliance, equality and voluntariness, separation of interest and fees, and alignment of quality and price when charging intermediary fees. If a commercial bank, by leveraging its dominant position, bundles loans to force customers to enter into intermediary business contracts but fails to provide substantive services, it constitutes a disguised collection of interest, deviates from the principles of equality, voluntariness, and fairness under civil law, increases corporate financing costs, and falls under the circumstance of 'charging fees without providing services' as defined in the Guidelines for Law Enforcement on Commercial Bank Charging Practices.
keywords_en: civil; financial loan contract dispute; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Shanghai; legal person; financial institution; Commercial Banking Law of the PRC; Contract Law of the PRC; determination of nature of intermediary fees; determination of disguised interest; calculation of overdue penalty interest; partial support; financial loan contract; syndicated loan; intermediary business charging; good faith; principle of fairness; contract dispute; loan contract; financial loan contract dispute of limited company, etc.
full_text_en:
China Huarong Asset Management Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Baoshan Sub-branch v. Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over financial loan contract

[Ruling Summary]

Commercial banks shall adhere to the principles of lawfulness and compliance, equality and voluntariness, separation of interest and fees, and matching of quality and price when charging intermediary fees. Where a commercial bank takes advantage of its dominant position to bundle loans and force customers to enter into intermediary business contracts without providing substantive services, this constitutes a disguised form of collecting interest, deviates from the principles of equality, voluntariness, and fairness under civil law, increases the financing costs of enterprises, and falls within the circumstance of "charging fees without providing services" as stipulated in the Guidelines on Law Enforcement of Commercial Bank Fee Charging.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2019) Supreme People's Court Final Civil Case No. 78

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 1869, 1st Floor, Building 5, No. 556 Liuyuan Road, Putuo District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Tang Guan, Executive Director of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wang Xin, employee of the Company.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Huarong Asset Management Co., Ltd., Shanghai Pilot Free Trade Zone Branch, domiciled at Room A-522, No. 188 Yesheng Road, China (Shanghai) Pilot Free Trade Zone.
Person in Charge: Gao Bo, General Manager of the Branch.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Chunfu, lawyer of Shanghai Allbright Law Offices.
Agent ad litem: Yang Bin, lawyer of Shanghai Allbright Law Offices.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Shanghai Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Baoshan Sub-branch, domiciled at No. 1198 Mudanjiang Road, Baoshan District, Shanghai.
Person in Charge: Yang Xinghua, President of the Sub-branch.
Agent ad litem: Zhou Qi, employee of the Sub-branch.
Agent ad litem: Shen Jun, employee of the Sub-branch.

Defendant at First Instance: Zhifu Enterprise Development (Group) Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 1917, 1st Floor, Building 5, No. 556 Liuyuan Road, Putuo District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Yan Baoming, Executive Director of the Company.

Defendant at First Instance: Ding Qinfu, male, born on January 16, 1962, Han ethnicity, residing in Changning District, Shanghai.

Defendant at First Instance: Yan Yuewen, female, born on September 8, 1965, Han ethnicity, residing in Changning District, Shanghai.

In the case of the appeal filed by Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhifu Maocheng) against the respondents China Huarong Asset Management Co., Ltd., Shanghai Pilot Free Trade Zone Branch (hereinafter referred to as Huarong Asset), Shanghai Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Baoshan Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Rural Commercial Bank), and the defendants at first instance Zhifu Enterprise Development (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhifu Development), Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen concerning a dispute over a financial loan contract, the appellant appealed against the civil judgment (2018) Hu Min Chu Zi No. 3 of the Shanghai High People's Court to this Court. After this Court accepted the case on January 15, 2019, it formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing. During the second-instance trial, the original respondent, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Co., Ltd., Shanghai Branch Business Department (hereinafter referred to as ICBC), applied to change its litigation subject status to Huarong Asset, and submitted to the court the Asset Transfer Agreement, the Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement, and corresponding transfer notices. As Zhifu Maocheng, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen were aware of the above transfer, this Court allowed the change of subject to Huarong Asset. The agent ad litem of the appellant Zhifu Maocheng, Ding Xin, the agents ad litem of the respondent Huarong Asset, Zhang Chunfu and Yang Bin, and the agent ad litem of Rural Commercial Bank, Zhou Qi, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen, having been summoned by summons of this Court, failed to appear without justifiable reasons and were deemed to have withdrawn their appeal, and the trial proceeded by default. After the legally extended trial period, this case has now been concluded.

Zhifu Maocheng's appeal requests: (1) Revoke item 1 of the first-instance judgment, and amend the judgment to deduct RMB 45.38 million from the loan principal that Zhifu Maocheng is required to repay to ICBC (calculated based on this amount temporarily, subject to the final amount confirmed by the court's judgment); (2) Revoke item 2 of the first-instance judgment, and amend the judgment to find that Zhifu Maocheng is not required to pay overdue penalty interest to ICBC, and that the relevant interest shall be calculated from March 21, 2018, at the interest rate agreed in the original contract; and that the interest corresponding to the principal amount of RMB 45.38 million that Zhifu Maocheng has repaid in installments from July 2011 to September 2014 shall be deducted, and the overpaid interest shall be deducted from the principal; (3) Revoke item 4 of the first-instance judgment, and amend the judgment to find that Zhifu Maocheng is not required to pay overdue penalty interest to Rural Commercial Bank, and that the relevant interest shall be calculated from March 21, 2018, at the interest rate agreed in the original contract; (4) Order ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank to bear the first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 5,584,771.66; (5) Order ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank to bear the second-instance case acceptance fee. Facts and reasons: (1) The first-instance judgment that the RMB 45.38 million paid by Zhifu Maocheng could not be offset against the loan principal in dispute lacked basic facts and legal basis and should be amended. The RMB 45.38 million paid by Zhifu Maocheng to ICBC should be included in the loan principal. Although such fees were nominally "service fees," "custody fees," "arrangement fees," etc., the signing of the relevant agreements and the remarks on the payment vouchers were all done under the strong request of ICBC. Such fees were not genuinely incurred "arrangement fees," "custody fees," etc., and the loan transaction in question did not constitute substantive paid services. Although the relevant agreements existed, they did not reflect the true intention of Zhifu Maocheng. (2) ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank's repeated collection of syndicated loan arrangement fees violated the regulations of the China Banking Regulatory Commission. (3) Zhifu Maocheng, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen should not bear overdue penalty interest and the first-instance litigation costs. ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank failed to disburse the full loan amount as agreed, constituting a breach of contract. Zhifu Maocheng did not breach the contract and should not bear overdue penalty interest and first-instance litigation costs.

The respondent Huarong Asset replied in defense: The first-instance court found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. It requests that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be upheld. (1) The RMB 45.38 million constitutes fees of a different nature and does not constitute the repayment principal of the loan in dispute. It pertains to a different legal relationship from the subject matter of this case. (2) The Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China provides that banks may charge handling fees. 1. Regarding the syndicated loan arrangement fee. According to the Guidelines for Syndicated Loans and the Convention on Syndicated Loan Intermediary Business, syndicated loan fees are fees paid by the borrower in addition to loan interest. The loan involved in this case amounted to as much as 1.5 billion yuan, which a single bank could hardly provide. Therefore, ICBC, as the lead arranger, organized other participating banks to provide loans to the borrower for this syndicated loan, successfully formed the syndicate, and provided substantive services. 2. Regarding the fund custody fee. The custody service involved included, in addition to fund transfer, services such as fund management and guarantee provided by ICBC to each payment to the corresponding construction unit and company at the request of Zhifu Maocheng. This was different from ordinary loan disbursement and constituted a value-added service. 3. Regarding the trade finance service fee. This is unrelated to this case. 4. Regarding the financial advisory fee. The work record sheet in the supplementary evidence of the first instance showed that Zhifu Maocheng was satisfied with the services provided by ICBC. Moreover, the legal relationship underlying such fee is also unrelated to this case. 5. Regarding the international financial service fee. This is another legal relationship between ICBC and Zhifu Maocheng and is completely unrelated to this case. (3) Overdue interest is expressly stipulated in the contract. Zhifu Maocheng has seriously breached the contract and should pay overdue interest.

The respondent Rural Commercial Bank replied in defense: Zhifu Maocheng breached the contract. The first-instance court's requirement that it bear corresponding liability and interest in accordance with the contract is legally sound. The collection of the syndicated loan arrangement fee is unrelated to Rural Commercial Bank, which did not receive such fee.

ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank filed the following claims with the first-instance court: 1. Order Zhifu Maocheng to immediately pay loan principal of RMB 738,282,000 (the same currency unit applies below) to ICBC, and at the same time, require it to pay overdue interest at the overdue penalty interest rate of 8.232% on the basis of the outstanding principal of RMB 738,282,000 from March 21, 2018, until the date of actual repayment (if the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China is adjusted, the overdue penalty interest rate shall be adjusted in accordance with the provisions of the Syndicated Loan Agreement involved); 2. Order Zhifu Maocheng to immediately pay loan principal of RMB 369,151,000 to Rural Commercial Bank, and at the same time, require it to pay overdue interest at the overdue penalty interest rate of 8.232% on the basis of the outstanding principal of RMB 369,151,000 from March 21, 2018, until the date of actual repayment (if the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China is adjusted, the overdue penalty interest rate shall be adjusted in accordance with the provisions of the Syndicated Loan Agreement involved); 3. Order Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen to bear joint and several suretyship liability for the debts in items 1 and 2 above of Zhifu Maocheng; 4. Order Zhifu Maocheng to provide mortgage security for the debts in items 1 and 2 above with the properties under its name, namely, floors B1-B4 and floors 1-4 of Building No. 21, Lane 318, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, and the basement level 4 car park and civil air defense car park of Building No. 21, Lane 318, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, and determine that if Zhifu Maocheng fails to repay the debts in items 1 and 2 above, ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank are entitled to be repaid on a priority basis from the proceeds obtained from the discount or auction/sale of the above mortgaged properties within the scope of the guarantee; 5. Order Zhifu Maocheng to provide mortgage security for the debts in items 1 and 2 above with the properties under its name, namely, floors 4-26 of Building No. 105, Lane 209, Zhenda Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, floors 1-25 of Building No. 118, Lane 368, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, floors 4-16 of Building No. 18, Lane 368, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, and floors 4-16 of Building No. 88, Lane 368, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, and determine that if Zhifu Maocheng fails to repay the debts in items 1 and 2 above, ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank are entitled to be repaid on a priority basis from the proceeds obtained from the discount or auction/sale of the above mortgaged properties within the scope of the guarantee; 6. The litigation costs of this case shall be jointly borne by Zhifu Maocheng, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen.

The first instance found the following facts: On March 11, 2011, ICBC, Rural Commercial Bank, and Zhifu Maocheng signed a Syndicated Loan Agreement, stipulating that each lender, severally and not jointly, agreed to provide the borrower with a loan of up to RMB 1.5 billion in total under the terms and conditions of the agreement. The loan term was 8 years, from the first drawdown date to the loan maturity date, tentatively from March 31, 2011, to March 30, 2019. Section 9.02 of the agreement stipulated the interest rate and interest calculation. (i) The contract interest rate was determined as the benchmark interest rate of the corresponding tier of the People's Bank of China (i.e., benchmark loan interest rate for over 5 years) plus 20%. The contract interest rate for each drawdown was calculated separately and adjusted periodically, with one year as a period. (iv) If the People's Bank of China adjusted the interest rate or the method of determining the interest rate, the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China shall apply. Section 9.03 of the Syndicated Loan Agreement stipulated penalty interest. (i) Overdue penalty interest. During the term of this agreement, if the borrower fails to pay on time the whole or part of the principal, interest, or any other amounts payable in connection with the loan that are due and payable or declared due and payable by the loan agent, then from the date such amounts become payable, overdue interest shall be calculated based on the actual overdue amount and the actual overdue days. The annual interest rate for such overdue interest shall be 140% of the loan interest rate applicable at the time of the overdue event as described in this agreement, and shall be paid immediately by the borrower upon request of the loan agent. Section 21.01 of the Syndicated Loan Agreement stipulated the composition of events of default. (i) Failure to pay. The borrower fails to pay immediately when any principal, interest, fees, or any other amounts payable between the borrower and the lenders under this agreement become due or are explicitly demanded. For the avoidance of doubt, the applicable penalty interest under Section 9.03 of this agreement shall commence from the date any amount under this agreement becomes due and payable but remains unpaid. Section 21.02 of the Syndicated Loan Agreement stipulated the consequences of default. Upon the occurrence of any event of default, the borrower shall promptly notify the loan agent, and each lender is entitled to issue written instructions to the loan agent, and the loan agent shall notify the borrower in writing in accordance with the lenders' instructions to exercise the following rights: (i) cease disbursing any loan at any time, declare any undrawn portion of the loan cancelled, and the lenders shall no longer have any obligation to provide loans to the borrower; and/or (ii) declare all loans immediately due and payable (at which time such loans, together with accrued interest and any other amounts then owed by the borrower under this agreement, shall become due and payable); and/or (iii) exercise any rights under the loan documents, including but not limited to disposing of the mortgaged real estate or exercising related rights; and/or (iv) collect penalty interest in accordance with the provisions of this agreement.

On April 21, 2011, ICBC, as the security agent, and Zhifu Maocheng signed the Real Estate Mortgage Agreement, stipulating that Zhifu Maocheng would provide mortgage security for the syndicated loan granted by ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank with the properties under its name, namely, floors B1-B4 and floors 1-4 of Building No. 21, Lane 318, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, and the basement level 4 car park and civil air defense car park of Building No. 21, Lane 318, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, and completed the mortgage registration on April 22, 2011. The registration certificate number Pu 201107006745's attached remarks of the Shanghai Real Estate Registration Certificate stated: mortgage of building under construction.

On December 2, 2011, ICBC, as the security agent, and Zhifu Maocheng signed the Real Estate Mortgage Agreement, stipulating that Zhifu Maocheng would provide mortgage security for the syndicated loan granted by ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank with the properties under its name, namely, floors 4-26 of Building No. 105, Lane 209, Zhenda Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, floors 1-25 of Building No. 118, Lane 368, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, floors 4-16 of Building No. 18, Lane 368, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, and floors 4-16 of Building No. 88, Lane 368, Gulu Road, Putuo District, Shanghai, and completed the mortgage registration on December 30, 2011. The registration certificate number Pu 201107019151's attached remarks of the Shanghai Real Estate Registration Certificate stated: mortgage of building under construction.

On March 30, 2015, ICBC, as the security agent, and Zhifu Development signed the Guarantee Agreement with contract number 01114000327101, whereby Zhifu Development voluntarily provided joint and several liability guarantee for the syndicated loan granted by ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank to Zhifu Maocheng. On March 30, 2015, ICBC, as the security agent, and Ding Qinfu and Yan Yuewen signed the Guarantee Agreement with contract number 01114000327102, whereby Ding Qinfu and Yan Yuewen voluntarily provided joint and several liability guarantee for the syndicated loan granted by ICBC and Rural Commercial Bank to Zhifu Maocheng.

From April 2011 to December 2015, ICBC disbursed loan amounts of RMB 808.34 million to Zhifu Maocheng, and Rural Commercial Bank disbursed loan amounts of RMB 404.18 million to Zhifu Maocheng.

On January 9, 2013, March 30, 2015, and March 30, 2017, ICBC, Rural Commercial Bank, Zhifu Maocheng, and others signed three Supplemental Agreements to Syndicated Loan Agreement, adjusting the repayment schedule three times.

During the trial, ICBC stated that Zhifu Maocheng had repaid principal of RMB 70,058,000 to it, and there was no interest overdue as of March 20, 2018. Rural Commercial Bank stated that Zhifu Maocheng had repaid principal of RMB 35,029,000 to it, and there was no interest overdue as of March 20, 2018. Zhifu Maocheng, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen all confirmed this.

The first instance also found: Zhifu Maocheng submitted 16 payment vouchers to prove that it had repaid loan principal of RMB 45.38 million to ICBC. However, the purpose column of the payment vouchers did not record "repayment of loan principal" but recorded purposes such as "capital arrangement fee," "custody fee," and "syndicated arrangement fee." Although Zhifu Maocheng argued that the purpose of the fee items was filled in at the request of ICBC, it did not deny the authenticity of ICBC's rebuttal evidence. In the relevant agreements adduced by ICBC, Zhifu Maocheng undertook to pay "syndicated loan arrangement fee," "custody fee," and other fees to ICBC.

The first-instance court held that the Syndicated Loan Agreement, the Real Estate Mortgage Agreement, the Guarantee Agreement, and the Supplemental Agreements to Syndicated Loan Agreement signed by ICBC, Rural Commercial Bank, and Zhifu Maocheng, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen were all true expressions of the parties' intentions, legal and valid, and all parties should abide by the agreements and perform their respective obligations. ICBC claimed that it had collected the relevant arrangement fees, custody fees, etc. based on the syndicated loan project and had fully adduced evidence. The first-instance court confirmed this based on facts. Furthermore, Zhifu Maocheng claimed that the fees illegally collected by ICBC should be calculated together as principal and interest in this case. It can be seen that Zhifu Maocheng also knew that the amounts recorded in the payment vouchers were not actually repayment of the loan in dispute. The payment fees adduced by it after trial clearly belong to a different legal relationship from the loan in dispute and cannot be offset as repaid principal.

After ICBC and SRCB released the loans as agreed, during the performance of the Syndicated Loan Agreement, Zhifu Maocheng failed to repay the principal of the syndicated loan due on September 30, 2017 and December 25, 2017 in accordance with the Syndicated Loan Agreement and the Syndicated Loan Supplemental Agreement, constituting a default. Based on the provisions of the Syndicated Loan Agreement regarding the consequences of default, on December 26, 2017, ICBC and SRCB declared that any undrawn portion of the loan was cancelled, and simultaneously declared that the entire loan became immediately due and payable, requiring Zhifu Maocheng to immediately pay ICBC and SRCB all outstanding principal and corresponding interest. This had contractual basis and was not contrary to law. Based on the evidence submitted by the parties, the court of first instance confirmed that from April 2011 to December 2015, ICBC disbursed loan funds of RMB 808,340,000 to Zhifu Maocheng, and SRCB disbursed loan funds of RMB 404,180,000 to Zhifu Maocheng. During the performance, Zhifu Maocheng repaid principal of RMB 70,058,000 to ICBC, and as of March 20, 2018, there was no outstanding interest. Zhifu Maocheng repaid principal of RMB 35,029,000 to SRCB, and as of March 20, 2018, there was no outstanding interest. Zhifu Maocheng, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen confirmed the above loan and repayment amounts during the court hearing. Although after the hearing, Zhifu Maocheng submitted evidence claiming that the RMB 45,380,000 it had paid to ICBC should be deducted from the disputed loan principal, this portion of the payment pertains to a different legal relationship from the disputed loan in this case and cannot be deducted as principal repaid. The court of first instance did not accept this claim. Zhifu Maocheng, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen argued that changes in government policies affected their ability to repay on time, and that this case should apply the principle of changed circumstances to fairly modify the repayment period agreed in the contract, and to dismiss the claims of ICBC and SRCB. The court of first instance held that the parties have the responsibility to provide evidence to prove the facts on which their claims are based or to rebut the facts on which the opposing party's claims are based. If there is no evidence or the evidence is insufficient to prove the party's factual assertions, the party bearing the burden of proof shall bear the adverse consequences. In this case, Zhifu Maocheng, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen did not submit sufficient and valid evidence to prove their claims, so the court of first instance did not accept them.

The Real Estate Mortgage Agreement signed between ICBC, as the security agent, and Zhifu Maocheng was legally established and became effective. After the mortgage registration of the mortgaged properties was completed, the relevant mortgage rights were legally established. Now that Zhifu Maocheng has failed to repay, ICBC and SRCB are entitled to require Zhifu Maocheng to bear the mortgage security liability.

ICBC, as the security agent, signed Guarantee Agreements with Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen respectively. Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen voluntarily provided joint and several liability guarantees for the syndicated loan disbursed by ICBC and SRCB to Zhifu Maocheng. As guarantors, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen shall bear joint and several guarantee liability in accordance with the agreements. Under the circumstances where Zhifu Maocheng failed to repay, the claims of ICBC and SRCB that Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen bear joint and several liability for repayment of Zhifu Maocheng's obligations are in accordance with the contract and legal provisions, and the court of first instance should support them. After bearing the guarantee liability, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen have the right to seek recourse from Zhifu Maocheng.

In summary, the court of first instance ruled: 1. Zhifu Maocheng shall pay ICBC the loan principal of RMB 738,282,000 within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect; 2. Zhifu Maocheng shall pay ICBC overdue interest from March 21, 2018 to the date of actual repayment (calculated on the principal of RMB 738,282,000 at the overdue penalty interest rate of 8.232%; if the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China is adjusted, the overdue penalty interest rate shall be adjusted in accordance with the relevant Syndicated Loan Agreement); 3. Zhifu Maocheng shall pay SRCB the loan principal of RMB 369,151,000 within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect; 4. Zhifu Maocheng shall pay SRCB overdue interest from March 21, 2018 to the date of actual repayment (calculated on the principal of RMB 369,151,000 at the overdue penalty interest rate of 8.232%; if the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China is adjusted, the overdue penalty interest rate shall be adjusted in accordance with the relevant Syndicated Loan Agreement); 5. If Zhifu Maocheng fails to perform the payment obligations in items 1, 2, 3, and 4 above, ICBC and SRCB have the right to seek priority in compensation from the properties registered under the Shanghai Real Estate Registration Certificates with registration certificate numbers Pu 201107006745 and Pu 201107019151 either by discounting the properties, or by auction or sale of the mortgaged properties. After the mortgaged properties are discounted, auctioned, or sold, any excess over the claim amount shall belong to Zhifu Maocheng, and any shortfall shall be further satisfied by Zhifu Maocheng; 6. Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen shall bear joint and several liability for Zhifu Maocheng's payment obligations in items 1, 2, 3, and 4 above. After bearing the guarantee liability, Zhifu Development, Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen have the right to seek recourse from Zhifu Maocheng.

During the second instance, none of the parties submitted new evidence. In addition to confirming the facts found by the first instance, this court further finds, based on the evidence undisputed by the parties during cross-examination in the first instance, as follows:

Regarding the syndicated arrangement fee of RMB 34,050,000. On March 11, 2011, the Syndicated Loan Agreement signed between ICBC and Zhifu Maocheng stipulated that borrower Zhifu Maocheng shall pay ICBC syndicated fees, including legal service fees and other expenses incurred by ICBC for the negotiation, preparation, drafting, and execution of the syndicated loan, as well as reasonable cost expenses for supplementing and revising the agreement text to protect the interests of ICBC and SRCB, including but not limited to appraisal, audit, registration, notarization, insurance, etc. On March 14, 2011, Zhifu Maocheng issued a Letter of Commitment for Payment of Syndicated Loan Arrangement Fee to ICBC. The letter stated that Zhifu Maocheng entrusted ICBC as arranger and lead bank to organize and arrange a syndicated loan with a total amount not exceeding RMB 1.5 billion (RMB 1,500,000,000.00) for the "East Side B1-9 Plot of Jinguang Business District (Phase II Commercial Premises of Zhifu Mingpin City) Development Project," and that the syndicate had been established and all parties had signed loan documents including the RMB 1.5 Billion Syndicated Loan Agreement (Contract No. 20110311). Zhifu Maocheng committed to pay ICBC a syndicated arrangement fee of RMB 50,000,000 in twelve installments from March 31, 2011 to December 21, 2013. The commitment letter also stated that the signing and submission of the commitment letter constitutes one of the conditions precedent for the first drawdown under the loan agreement, and the commitment letter shall be part of the loan documents. Once Zhifu Maocheng violates any matter under the commitment letter, it will be deemed a breach of the loan agreement, and ICBC has the right to declare the loan in default and take corresponding default remedies according to the provisions of the loan agreement. Later, between March 2011 and June 2014, Zhifu Maocheng paid a total of RMB 34,050,000 in syndicated loan arrangement fees in nine installments.

Regarding the fund custody fee of RMB 5,820,000. On March 21, 2011, Zhifu Maocheng and ICBC signed the Loan Fund Custody Agreement. Subsequently, on July 28, 2011, Zhifu Maocheng paid ICBC a custody fee of RMB 1,220,000. On June 25, 2013, Zhifu Maocheng and ICBC signed the Secure Account (Customer Fund) Custody Agreement. Subsequently, on June 27, 2013, Zhifu Maocheng paid ICBC a custody fee of RMB 2,600,000. On December 17, 2013, Zhifu Maocheng and ICBC signed the Secure Account (Customer Fund) Custody Agreement. Subsequently, on December 31, 2013, Zhifu Maocheng paid ICBC a custody fee of RMB 2,000,000. The above agreements stipulated that ICBC provides fund custody services for Zhifu Maocheng regarding the syndicated loan involved in the case.

Regarding the trade finance service fee of RMB 1,360,000. On December 17, 2013, Zhifu Maocheng and ICBC signed the Trade Finance Service Agreement, stipulating that ICBC provides comprehensive financial services to Zhifu Maocheng, including commercial credit investigation and commodity inventory management. Subsequently, on April 8, 2013 and December 31, 2013, Zhifu Maocheng paid ICBC trade finance arrangement fees of RMB 510,000 and RMB 850,000 respectively.

Regarding the financial advisory fee of RMB 3,000,000. On December 17, 2013, Zhifu Maocheng and ICBC signed the Financial Advisory Service Agreement, stipulating that ICBC provides financial advisory services to Zhifu Maocheng for the "Phase II of Zhifu Mingpin City" project. Subsequently, on September 10, 2014, Zhifu Maocheng paid ICBC a financial advisory fee of RMB 3,000,000.

Regarding the international business service fee of RMB 1,150,000. On December 17, 2013, Zhifu Maocheng and ICBC signed the ICBC International Business Comprehensive Service Agreement, stipulating that ICBC provides professional services related to international business to Zhifu Maocheng, including international risk consultation, information inquiry on overseas banks and foreign counterparties, and assistance in selecting the best settlement method for international trade. Subsequently, on December 31, 2013, Zhifu Maocheng paid ICBC an international business service fee of RMB 1,150,000.

In addition, when Zhifu Maocheng paid ICBC the total of RMB 45,380,000, comprising the above syndicated arrangement fee of RMB 34,050,000, fund custody fee of RMB 5,820,000, trade finance service fee of RMB 1,360,000, financial advisory fee of RMB 3,000,000, and international business service fee of RMB 1,150,000, it had no overdue interest on the syndicated loan.

This court holds that the issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether Zhifu Maocheng should bear overdue penalty interest; 2. Whether the RMB 45,380,000 paid by Zhifu Maocheng to ICBC can be deducted from the disputed loan principal.

(1) Regarding whether Zhifu Maocheng should bear overdue penalty interest

Zhifu Maocheng appealed that it did not default and should not bear overdue penalty interest. In this case, the Syndicated Loan Agreement and the Syndicated Loan Supplemental Agreement are true expressions of the parties' intentions, legally valid and effective, and all parties shall perform corresponding obligations in accordance with the agreements. According to the facts found in the first instance, during the performance of its obligations, Zhifu Maocheng failed to repay the principal of the syndicated loan due on September 30, 2017 and December 25, 2017 in accordance with the Syndicated Loan Supplemental Agreement, which constitutes a factual default. According to Article 9.03 of the Syndicated Loan Agreement on penalty interest, in the event that Zhifu Maocheng fails to repay on time, ICBC and SRCB have the right to charge overdue interest based on the actual overdue amount and actual overdue days from the date the payment is due. The first instance judgment ordering Zhifu Maocheng to pay overdue interest to ICBC and SRCB has factual and legal basis and is not improper.

(2) Regarding whether the RMB 45,380,000 paid by Zhifu Maocheng to ICBC can be deducted from the disputed loan principal

First, the disputed RMB 45,380,000 and the loan involved in the case arise from the same legal relationship. The relevant syndicated arrangement fee, fund custody fee, trade finance service fee, financial advisory fee, and international business service fee were all contracted under relevant agreements after the signing of the Syndicated Loan Agreement and the Syndicated Loan Supplemental Agreement in this case and during the performance period of the said contracts. Zhifu Maocheng also paid the corresponding amounts during this period. Moreover, the above fees all arose from the financial loan contract dispute in this case. There was no other business dealings between ICBC and Zhifu Maocheng other than the financial loan dispute involved in the case. The above syndicated arrangement fees and other fees were all incurred due to the loan involved in the case. The people's court should review them.

Second, ICBC did not provide corresponding services such as syndicated arrangement, fund custody, trade finance services, financial advisory, and international business services. Article 9 of the Notice of the General Office of the National Development and Reform Commission on Issuing the Guidance on Law Enforcement of Commercial Bank Charging Practices (hereinafter referred to as the "Guidance on Law Enforcement of Commercial Bank Charging Practices") stipulates that commercial banks' charging practices shall follow the principles of lawfulness and compliance, equality and voluntariness, separation of interest and fees, and matching quality with price. Equality and voluntariness means that commercial banks and customers have equal legal status and should provide services on the basis of mutual voluntariness, and should not use financing or other transaction conditions as a prerequisite to force or covertly force the provision of services and collection of fees. Matching quality with price means that commercial banks should provide reasonably priced services based on the actual needs of customers. Businesses such as advisory and consulting, fund supervision, asset custody, and financing arrangement particularly should reflect the requirement of substantive services. In practice, banks use their advantageous position to bundle loans and force hidden interest or provide intermediary services, deviating from the principles of equality, voluntariness, and fairness in civil law and increasing the financing costs of real enterprises. Financial regulatory authorities have repeatedly issued documents to regulate and focus on rectifying this chronic problem. To form a joint force between judiciary and administration, to play the role of judicial regulation and guidance, to promote a virtuous cycle between finance and the real economy, and to effectively reduce corporate financing costs, hidden interest and non-compliant fees charged by financial institutions must be strictly reviewed. In the second instance proceeding of this case, through court investigation, Zhifu Maocheng argued that ICBC did not provide syndicated loan services, fund custody services, trade finance services, financial advisory services, or international business comprehensive financial services. Apart from submitting the relevant agreements and contracts to the court, Huarong Asset also failed to provide evidence proving that ICBC had provided Zhifu Maocheng with the above services independent of the syndicated loan and with substantive content. It can be seen that ICBC did not provide substantive services, and the true intention between ICBC and Zhifu Maocheng was not to establish service contract relationships such as fund custody and advisory, but rather that ICBC used its advantageous position in lending to make unreasonable charges, indirectly increasing the enterprise's financing costs. This falls under the "charging without service" situation stipulated in the Guidance on Law Enforcement of Commercial Bank Charging Practices, so its collection of the RMB 45,380,000 fees involved in the case lacks factual basis.

Finally, the disputed RMB 45,380,000 should be deducted from the disputed principal. In the first instance proceeding, it was found that as of March 20, 2018, Zhifu Maocheng had no overdue interest owed to ICBC and SRCB. That is, when Zhifu Maocheng paid ICBC a total of RMB 45,380,000, consisting of the syndicated arrangement fee of RMB 34,050,000, fund custody fee of RMB 5,820,000, trade finance service fee of RMB 1,360,000, financial advisory fee of RMB 3,000,000, and international business service fee of RMB 1,150,000, it had not defaulted on the syndicated loan interest to the banks. If during the loan period, the borrower has paid the loan interest on time in accordance with the main loan contract and has also paid additional fees in the name of service fees under other contracts or agreements, then the court may allow such portion of fees to be deducted from the principal. Therefore, Zhifu Maocheng's claim to deduct the RMB 45,380,000 fee from the loan principal is supported by this court.

Furthermore, according to Article 3 of the Supplementary Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Acquisition and Disposal of Non-performing Bank Assets by Financial Asset Management Companies (Fa Fa [2005] No. 62), when the people's court learns of the fact of transfer of creditor's rights, the people's court may, upon application by the transferor or the transferee and a valid creditor's rights transfer agreement, rule to change the litigation subject. However, in this case, the creditor's rights had been transferred before the first instance, and the litigation subject should have been changed during the first instance. However, because the parties did not inform the first instance court of this fact, the first instance court still used the transferor as the litigation subject to render the judgment. Since the change of litigation subject in this case is caused by the legal act of creditor's rights transfer, the subject before and after the change is in a succession relationship. Therefore, after this court rules to change the litigation subject, the transferee, Huarong Asset, may enjoy the substantive rights of ICBC under the Asset Transfer Agreement. In summary, Zhifu Maocheng's appeal is partially upheld. In accordance with Article 144, Article 170, paragraph 1, items 1 and 2, and Article 174 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm item 3 of the judgment of the Shanghai High People's Court (2018) Hu Min Chu No. 3;

2. Reverse items 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6 of the judgment of the Shanghai High People's Court (2018) Hu Min Chu No. 3;

3. Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. shall pay China Huarong Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanghai Free Trade Zone Branch the loan principal of RMB 692,902,000 within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect;

4. Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. shall pay China Huarong Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanghai Free Trade Zone Branch overdue interest from March 21, 2018 to the date of actual repayment (calculated on the principal of RMB 692,902,000, with the overdue penalty interest rate according to the relevant Syndicated Loan Agreement, and the benchmark interest rate according to the one-year to five-year loan prime rate published by the National Interbank Funding Center for the corresponding period);

5. Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. shall pay Shanghai Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. Baoshan Branch overdue interest from March 21, 2018 to the date of actual repayment (calculated on the principal of RMB 369,151,000, with the overdue penalty interest rate according to the relevant Syndicated Loan Agreement, and the benchmark interest rate according to the one-year to five-year loan prime rate published by the National Interbank Funding Center for the corresponding period);

6. If Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. fails to perform its payment obligations, China Huarong Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanghai Free Trade Zone Branch and Shanghai Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. Baoshan Branch have the right to seek priority in compensation from the properties registered under the Shanghai Real Estate Registration Certificates with registration certificate numbers Pu 201107006745 and Pu 201107019151 either by discounting the properties, or by auction or sale of the mortgaged properties. After the mortgaged properties are discounted, auctioned, or sold, any excess over the claim amount shall belong to Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd., and any shortfall shall be further satisfied by Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd.;

7. Zhifu Enterprise Development (Group) Co., Ltd., Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen shall bear joint and several guarantee liability for Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd.'s payment obligations in items 1, 3, 4, and 5 above. After bearing the guarantee liability, Zhifu Enterprise Development (Group) Co., Ltd., Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen have the right to seek recourse from Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd.;

8. Dismiss the other appeal claims of Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the debt shall be doubled for delayed performance in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 5,584,771.66; property preservation fee: RMB 5,000; total: RMB 5,589,771.66. China Huarong Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanghai Free Trade Zone Branch bears RMB 219,970.19; Shanghai Zhifu Maocheng Real Estate Co., Ltd., Zhifu Enterprise Development (Group) Co., Ltd., Ding Qinfu, and Yan Yuewen jointly bear RMB 5,369,801.47. Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 268,700, borne by China Huarong Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanghai Free Trade Zone Branch.

This judgment is final.
